chapter: Mario Bauza and the Cuban sextets
title: Meeting Mario Bauza and his musical training
summary: Machito met Mario at Pobolote through his sister Estela; Mario was a trained clarinetist taught by Hugo Cien and Arturo Andrade.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: I see. Macho, there came a time where your father moved to the cigar makers' projects in Pobolote and you met Mario Bauza. Tell me, how did that come about? What do you remember about that day?
Well, it was a beautiful thing.
I was about sixteen. Estela was about twelve and Mario was about fourteen. I am older than Mario two years; but Mario was an accomplished musician. He was playing with the Philharmonic.
Oh yes, Mario he was graduated when he was eleven or twelve.
Had you been into music before meeting Mario?

Yes, so Mario had one of the best teachers in the country. He was a top ten clarinet player, Hugo Cien, and his godfather, Arturo Andrade, he was a musician in the - for the army - army band, a good musician, so in order he could kill time in Pabolote, he opened a school of music, free; so Mario used to sing by ear all the lessons, when he was seven, so he says: 'Oh yeah, you could sing by ear the lesson? - ah ------
You mean like Do - Re - Mi

Yeah, Do - Re - Mi - and Mario used to know practically the whole book of solfeggio or solfeggia and he forced Mario to read and make himself a musician where he start that he know really to to Hugo Cien and then he went to the Municipal Academy. Oh, as a matter of fact, about two or three months, he received all his - all his papers from the Academy of Music in Cuba.
